players.product: Niche DRAM (DDR4, DDR3L, LPDDR4X) plus NOR flash and SLC NAND flash (fabless)

quarterly_data.signal: Vice chairman and general manager He Wei (Q1 2026 results briefing): helped by tightening memory supply and further price rises, Q1 2026 revenue rose 119.38% year on year to RMB 41.88 hundred million, up 76.6% quarter on quarter; net profit attributable rose 522.79% to RMB 14.61 hundred million, up 158.7% quarter on quarter; gross margin rose 12.17 percentage points quarter on quarter to 57.08%, driven by memory price increases.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 2026 revenue RMB 41.88 hundred million (+119.38% YoY, +76.6% QoQ); net profit RMB 14.61 hundred million (+522.79%); gross margin 57.08%

quarterly_data.signal: Product lines in Q1 2026 (results briefing): board secretary Dong Lingyan said DRAM revenue more than doubled quarter on quarter; He Wei said NOR Flash revenue grew well quarter on quarter mainly on volume, with fast share gains in automotive, optical modules, edge AI and domestic servers, SLC NAND Flash revenue grew strongly quarter on quarter and its share of total revenue rose sharply, and MCU revenue rose sharply quarter on quarter on industrial, consumer and automotive demand, strong demand in AI peripherals, new-energy peripherals and innovative consumer products, and normal customer restocking - a trend he expects to continue in Q2. He Wei: as supply-chain costs rose the company had to negotiate MCU price increases with customers broadly in Q1, and customers are raising safety stock, continuing in Q2; it plans AI MCUs with an integrated NPU for automation, digital energy and AIoT. Analog subsidiary Suzhou Saixin had Q1 revenue of about RMB 6,500 ten-thousand with gross margin above 50%, the company's own analog business nearly RMB 2,000 ten-thousand (up 15% quarter on quarter); sensor revenue fell quarter on quarter on weak downstream demand.
quarterly_data.figure: Suzhou Saixin Q1 revenue about RMB 6,500 ten-thousand; own analog nearly RMB 2,000 ten-thousand (+15% QoQ)

quarterly_data.signal: Outlook (results briefing): VP and CFO Sun Guijing said the company expects niche DRAM and SLC NAND Flash prices to keep rising this year and NOR Flash prices to keep rising mildly; memory gross margin improved over recent quarters partly because foundry and other cost increases lag price increases, and as prices level off and supply-side costs rise she expects memory gross margin to become relatively stable or even fall back moderately. Board secretary Dong Lingyan: NOR Flash supply is relatively tight, fast-growing server-related demand is crowding out other uses, and mild price rises should continue this year. The company: niche DRAM contract prices have risen for about 1 year amid severe supply tightness. He Wei on demand: edge AI relatively strong; industrial recovering, with power, optical modules and robots strong; automotive steady; consumer demand suppressed by upstream price rises.

DRAM roadmap (results briefing): He Wei said two new parts - a small-capacity LPDDR4 and a new-process DDR4 8Gb - taped out at the start of the year and, if testing and sampling go smoothly, are expected to enter volume production in H2 2026. Board secretary Dong Lingyan: the DRAM line-up centres on DDR4 8Gb and DDR4 4Gb, the coming LPDDR4 will lean toward 2GB capacity, and DDR3 wafer starts stopped from the middle of last year so its revenue contribution will keep shrinking. Customised memory (subsidiary Qingyun Technology) projects in car cockpits, AI PCs and robots are expected to reach mass production this year; the business is still in market development and a low share of revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: LPDDR4 and new-process DDR4 8Gb volume production expected H2 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity (results briefing): He Wei said SLC NAND capacity has expanded since the start of the year and is expected to grow further, slowly, in H2; the company is negotiating with capacity providers to expand and is developing higher-capacity products, after quickly opening up the niche 2D NAND market as international majors shifted capacity to 3D NAND from 2025. NOR Flash capacity expansion with supplier partners is steady and controlled, not a large expansion. The company said all its memory products benefited from the shortage in Q1, with volume and price both rising.
